subject: Deal-gated scaling runbook: firming OEM lead times & cloud burst choreography
messages:
From: Priya Shah <procurement@acme.ai>
To: neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity schedule + OEM lead times for RDW-ACME-2027-09

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Acme is excited to move forward but we need to lock the capacity on the delivery timeline side so procurement can schedule payments and our infra team can plan cluster migrations. Short summary of asks: 

- Confirm confirmed profile: 250 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs (mix of reserved + burst) across two regions (us-west, us-east) by Oct 1 2027.
- Provide OEM lead-time window for quoted hardware (OmniOEM part numbers in the attached RFQ). We need a firm ETA range (best / typical / worst) to include in our SOW.
- Outline cloud-burst fallback: if OEM can’t deliver, what’s the contractual path to burst into cloud capacity (Azure/GCP) and estimated time to onboard burst capacity at scale?

Can you share an action plan and owners for each ask? Procurement is on a tight calendar — we need this packaged to present to Acme legal by May 7.

Attachments: Acme_RFQ_omnioem_v2.pdf (RFQ, vendor part numbers)

Priya Shah

Priya —

Thanks for the clear ask and the RFQ. I pulled together a short runbook that maps the procurement asks to owners, timelines, and fallbacks. High level: we propose a phased onramp (Phase 1: 80 reserved GPUs by 2027-08-15; Phase 2: additional 170 via mix of OEM deliveries + cloud-burst by 2027-10-01). That lets Acme begin integration and load testing while we finalize longer lead-time deliveries.

Key items I need from you by EOD May 3:
- Confirm whether Acme will accept a mixed-instance SLA (reserved + burst) in the SOW.
- Any vendor-preferred payment milestones or acceptance criteria that affect lead times.

I’ve attached: capacity_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook with timelines, owners, and rollback triggers) and acme_deal_capacity_matrix.xlsx (requested GPU mix).

We’ll own coordination with OmniOEM for the firm ETA and with Azure for the burst onboarding timeline. Marcus will scope the staging pool and quantization guidance to reduce peak unit counts while preserving performance.

Proposed next steps: 30-min sync with Proc + Infra + Vendors week of May 3. I’m free May 4–6 mornings PT.

+1 on phased approach. A few technical clarifications and suggestions to tighten the runbook: 

- Staging pool: propose 40 GPU staging cluster (same instance family) in us-west for image validation and KV cache warmup. Owner: Marcus. ETA: 3 weeks after Phase 1 signing.
- Quantization / perf tuning: If Acme allows a 10–15% quantization profile on the non-peak models, we can reduce required physical units for Phase 2 by ~25% — I put an optional column in the xlsx. Owner: Marcus (perf) / Neha (contract).
- OEM lead times: OmniOEM typically publishes lead windows in quarter buckets. We should push for a committed ship-week and an expedited penalty clause in the SOW for >12-week slips. Omnioem will need forecasted PO dates to give a firm commitment.

I’ll take point on the staging runbook and provide a more detailed ops checklist before the sync.

—Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Neha / Marcus,

Thanks for looping us in. We reviewed the target profile (250 GPUs across us-west/us-east). Quick notes on cloud-burst onboarding:

- Marketplace reserved/on-demand mix: we can provision burst pools within 5 business days after quota approval for initial 60–120 GPUs. For larger sustained bursts (100+ GPUs for >30 days) we need a committed capacity exchange which is typically 4–8 weeks.
- Quota process: please complete the attached Azure quota form (azure-quota-form.pdf) with the estimated vCPU/GPU SKU counts and expected start dates.
- Marketplace listing: https://marketplace.azure.com/items/redwood-inference — we can expedite listing changes if a partner AM is assigned.

If you want a formal written commitment, we can produce a capacity letter conditioned on Azure account validation and a purchase order.

Regards,
Gabe Turner

Priya — thanks everyone for the quick responses. This thread captures the agreed runbook and owners; I’m packaging this as the appendix to the SOW. Please treat the items below as the mutual action plan we want to show Acme legal on May 7.

Mutual action plan (owners / deadlines):
1) Phase 1 delivery (80 reserved GPUs) — Target ship/integration date: 2027-08-15. Owner: OmniOEM / Neha to confirm PO week by May 14.
2) Staging pool (40 GPUs, us-west) — Owner: Marcus. ETA: 3 weeks post Phase 1.
3) Phase 2 top-up (170 GPUs mix) — Target: 2027-10-01. Owner: OmniOEM + Redwood (Neha) / fallback: Azure burst.
4) Azure burst onboarding — Complete quota form by May 5 (Owner: Acme procurement). Azure estimates initial burst within 5 business days of approval for up to 120 GPUs; larger sustained capacity 4–8 weeks. Owner: Gabe (Azure).
5) Contractual protections — Neha to propose an expedited-shipment SLAs and penalty language for >12-week OEM slips by May 10.
6) Quantization optimization — Marcus to deliver optional profile and revised capacity excel by May 6 (this may reduce physical units required).

Open items for the May 4 sync:
- Acme confirmation on accepting mixed-instance SLOs and staged rollout.
- Final PO timing and payment milestones that affect OEM order placement.

Quoted earlier messages below for context. If this looks good I’ll mark attachments and links for inclusion in the SOW appendix and set up the May 4 09:00 PT call.

Thanks,
